<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **46** documentable anchor(s).

**55** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337`.

⛔ **13** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `sys_user (symbol, 49 pages)`, `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 49 pages)`
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **24** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `634c795da01973a771a6501c10280ba1b7a30f0d` — the merge of head `c5ca45e7c90f5aa580820821cefc1a5ae57d92f0` into base `87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 634c795da01973a771a6501c10280ba1b7a30f0d && git checkout 634c795da01973a771a6501c10280ba1b7a30f0d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337 c5ca45e7c90f5aa580820821cefc1a5ae57d92f0 && git checkout -B drift-repro 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337 && git merge --no-ff c5ca45e7c90f5aa580820821cefc1a5ae57d92f0

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 87d945873da8e13ae2b6ee5ac43c075203abc337` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位 ACCEPT · head `d2d101d02629971995804418e74be8a63ddfc8d8`

#31739 PR-1 (ADR-0151 D1 + D2). The changeset reads `Clause-②: yes` / `Metadata-protocol: none`, and the paths give no review face. The seat reviewed it at TIER_DEFAULT. Not governed: 0 of 23 paths hit the register.

- **D1 row guard** (`registerServiceAccountRowGuard`, priority 4, registered by both `AuthPlugin` and `IdentityObjectsPlugin`): insert and update are judged correctly for human, agent, empty and null. The kind is immutable. An agent row must name an existing person as owner, never itself, and a person row names none. Predicate updates dispatch `beforeUpdate` once per row with `previous`, so the `!previous` early return is not a way round the guard. Both columns are `readonly` and listed in `MANAGED_EXTENSION_FIELDS`.
- **D2 refusals:** `session.create.before` and `account.create.before` ask first, before the host hooks, on every sign-in method, impersonation and minted session.
- **Should-fix from this round, fixed at d2d101d0:** a failed `sys_user` read used to refuse every person with the AI-service-account message. It still fails closed, but now answers its own `USER_ROW_READ_FAULT_REFUSAL` (503 `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`, matching plugin-auth's existing read-fault answers). The cause is logged once, without the session or credential. Pins cover both doors, and three ablations went red and were restored.
- **Reconciler / backfill:** the new outcome `agent-account` is added to `ReconcileOutcome` (covered by `Clause-②: yes`), and the backfill skips agent rows.
- **Accepted deviations:** (1) the changeset is `patch`, following `Metadata-protocol: none` (ruling A on #25105). (2) Three forced edits in `first-session-membership-ordering.test.ts`, named in the body, which follow from failing closed. (3) No labels on the PR. (4) The ADR-0151 status line rides with PR-3; if the governed check refuses that, an amendment card is filed instead.

Uses `Part of #31739`. PR-2 (D3 + admission + inventory) starts from main after this lands. Landing: once CI is all green, check K, then relay `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
